judged_text: San Pedro de Atacama can be visited year-round, and its standard tours are available in every month, although summer storms and winter snow can close the high-altitude trips for a day or more. Those trips climb above 4,000 meters to the El Tatio geysers, the Altiplanic lagoons and the red rocks of Piedras Rojas. Valle de la Luna and the salt lagoons near town are much less exposed. If your dates are flexible, April, October and November offer the best overall balance. The summer storm season up high is over or has not begun, and snow is less likely than in winter. Nights in town average about 4 °C, although dawn at El Tatio can still be below zero. April afternoons are slightly cooler; October and November have longer days. May and September are colder, with average lows near freezing in town, and in September late snow can still close the high routes. From December to March, town afternoons are hot and nights mild, but storms can close the high roads; from June to August, dawns are coldest and snow can close them. Either way, put the high trip early in your stay, keep a spare day and check the weather up high the day before. Book rooms and tours earlier for January and February, the winter school break in late June or July, and the days around September 18, when many Chileans travel. In any month, see Valle de la Luna at sunset and El Tatio at dawn, and book stargazing when the Moon is down during the session.

history: Round 1 (3/3 FAIL): GENERAL-AS-UNIVERSAL x3 ('May and September also work' omitted September late snow); ADVICE-MECHANISM x3 ('To avoid the main Chilean holiday dates, skip ...' was circular; 'pack for nights around 1 to 2 C' packed to an average while May has 13 frost nights); TENDENCY-AS-RULE x2 (same packing line, decision row 'still dry'); PLAIN x2 (a 42-word four-clause sentence; El Tatio / Piedras Rojas unglossed); OVERCLAIM x1 ('about an hour more daylight' understated November's 98 minutes); SAFETY-PROMINENCE x1 (no action for June-August snow); SCOPE x1 (packing figure from the town station applied to El Tatio dawns). Fixes: September snow named; holiday line turned into book-ahead advice; packing figure replaced by 'average lows near freezing in town'; sentence split; El Tatio geysers and red rocks of Piedras Rojas glossed; daylight stated as 'longer days'; one 'put the high trip early, keep a spare day, check the weather up high the day before' instruction now covers both risk seasons.

Round 2 (1 PASS, 2 FAIL): OVERCLAIM x2 ('April is slightly cooler' - true of afternoons, not nights: April's average low 4.0 C vs October's 3.6 C); GENERAL-AS-UNIVERSAL x1 plus two pauses ('the July winter break' - the break is set by region and can start in late June). Fixes: 'April afternoons are slightly cooler'; 'the winter school break in late June or July'; decision row 'late June-July'; judge A's suggestion adopted that the Moon should be down 'during the session'.
